strings.name: Michael Jordan
strings.summary: Michael Jordan is an American basketball player who won six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls and five regular-season Most Valuable Player awards. Known for scoring, defense and performances in decisive games, he was also important to basketball’s global reach and the commercialization of athletes. His career included retirement, a move into baseball and two comebacks. He later entered team ownership and held a controlling interest in the Charlotte Hornets.
strings.coverageNote: Focuses on his playing career and his acquisition and sale of a controlling team interest in 2010 and 2023. Live business valuations are not tracked.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: The Bulls dynasty
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Six NBA championships and six Finals MVP awards form the core of his competitive achievements.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Influence beyond the court
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Alongside a college championship, Olympic gold medals and professional achievements, participated in team ownership and sports business.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Sells his controlling interest in the Hornets
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Completed the sale of a majority stake in the Charlotte Hornets, ending his period as controlling owner.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Becomes controlling owner of Charlotte’s team
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Acquired a controlling stake in the team then called the Bobcats, joining the ranks of NBA owners.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Enters the Basketball Hall of Fame
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in recognition of his professional achievements.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Ends his NBA playing career
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Completed his final season with the Washington Wizards, after making his second comeback in 2001.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Completes a second three-peat
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Helped the Bulls win consecutive titles from 1996 to 1998, taking his championship total to six.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Returns to the Chicago Bulls
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Ended his baseball stint and returned to the NBA, later leading the Bulls into a second championship era.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Retires for the first time
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Announced his retirement after the Bulls’ first three-peat, then joined a minor-league baseball team.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Wins his first NBA championship
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Led the Bulls to the franchise’s first title and won Finals MVP; added another Olympic gold medal the following year.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Enters the NBA and wins Olympic gold
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Selected third overall by the Bulls in the draft and won Olympic gold with the US team that same year.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Wins the college national championship
strings.timeline.event-10.text: As a North Carolina freshman, made a decisive basket in the NCAA final to help his team win the title.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in New York
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Brooklyn and raised in Wilmington, North Carolina.
